subject: Invoice/timestamp entropy: EU marketplace meter alignment & VAT routing
messages:
From: Pieter van Dijk <pieter@cloudmarketplace.eu>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lars Nielsen <lars@acme-clouds.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:14:00Z
Subject: Discrepancy on Nov invoice + VAT withholding

Hi Naomi,

We just received the Azure marketplace remittance for November and noticed ~€42k was held back for VAT. Our accounting matched the gross metered lines to the invoice but the timestamps in the Azure CSV don’t line up with our meter aggregation windows (UTC vs local). That mismatch appears to have caused Azure to attribute usage to a UK-listed entity rather than our NL entity; the VAT hold was applied as a result.

Short version: invoice references and your invoice ID 202611-AC have consistent amounts but the per-line attributions are shifting when the timestamp falls inside Azure’s rounding window. We need Redwood to confirm which entity you want the revenue mapped to and provide the prefix-aligned metering CSV so we can request a credit/adjustment with our marketplace provider.

Attaching the Azure invoice extract and a sample of the marketplace CSV (extracted columns). Can you confirm: 1) which Redwood legal entity should receive EUR invoices for Gridline/CloudMarket EU, and 2) whether Redwood has a preferred reallocation flow (credit memo vs. retrospective invoice).

Thanks,
Pieter
Billing ops | CloudMarket EU

Attachments: azure-invoice-202611.pdf (stub), marketplace-lines-202611.csv (stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T10:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Discrepancy on Nov invoice + VAT withholding

Team — forwarding Pieter from CloudMarket EU. They have a VAT withholding because the marketplace attributed charges to the wrong legal entity based on timestamp rounding. I think this is the same class of issue we saw in Q3 but with Azure’s new submission window it’s reappeared.

Action items:
- Jonas: can you run the ledger match for Gridline/CloudMarket EU against our ingested marketplace CSV (use run id RECON-202611-GME)? Compare the timestamp rounding rules and produce a small CSV with corrected attribution.
- Karthik: what’s the preferred flow for EU VAT reallocation here? Do we typically issue a credit + corrected invoice or request the marketplace to reissue? Any hard dependencies on entity-tax IDs?
- Marissa: if we move forward with a credit memo, what terms do we need (internal approval / finance tickets)?

I’ll reply to Pieter with a plan once we have the quick triage.

Naomi
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T14:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discrepancy on Nov invoice + VAT withholding

Naomi / team — ran the initial reconciliation. High-level findings:

- Root cause: Azure’s metering export has a rounding window that normalizes timestamps to the nearest minute in CET for EU marketplaces. Our ingestion pipeline treated timestamps as UTC and bucketed a small subset (~2.6% of lines) into the previous day for the Gridline account. That shifted ~€47k of usage into a UK entity mapping used by the marketplace connector.
- Quick fix: produce a prefix-aligned CSV using the marketplace’s expected CET-normalized timestamps (see attached redwood-ledger-recon-202611.xlsx).
- Recommended remediation: 1) submit the corrected CSV to CloudMarket EU and request a reallocation / credit memo from Azure, or 2) issue a negative invoice + corrected invoice if marketplace refuses reallocation. Option 1 is faster but requires marketplace acceptance and may take 10–14 business days.

I attached: redwood-ledger-recon-202611.xlsx (sample mapping), and a small log with the offending timestamp rows (metering-timestamp-sample.log).

I also flagged ingest pipeline task INGEST-537 to add a CET-normalization step for EU marketplace feeds. If Karthik confirms we should prefer marketplace reallocation, I’ll prepare the CSV in the exact column order their support portal expects.

Jonas
Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ledger-recon-202611.xlsx, metering-timestamp-sample.log

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Pieter van Dijk <pieter@cloudmarketplace.eu>, Azure Marketplace Billing <billing@microsoft.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T08:51:00Z
Subject: RE: Discrepancy on Nov invoice + VAT withholding

Hi Pieter — thanks for the heads up and the files. Apologies for the churn here. Quick summary of our plan below and proposed timeline: 

Plan:
1) Redwood will request reallocation with Azure/CloudMarket EU using a corrected CSV aligned to CET minute boundaries. We prefer the marketplace reallocation route (credit memo + reattribution) to avoid issuing retrospective invoices if possible.
2) Jonas has prepared the CSV and attached the reconciliation workbook; we will submit it to your marketplace billing contact and to Azure billing.
3) If Azure rejects reallocation, Redwood will issue a corrective negative invoice and reissue to the NL entity, then coordinate VAT reclaim with your team.

Timeline:
- Today (16 Dec): Redwood to upload corrected CSV to the CloudMarket EU support portal and open an official ticket with Azure billing (cc’d).
- By 22 Dec: Expect initial marketplace acceptance / acknowledgment. If accepted, Azure will process credit memo in the next payout cycle (target by end of Jan).
- If not accepted: Redwood finance will prepare the invoice/credit pair and Marissa will route for approval.

Please confirm CloudMarket EU’s preferred support ticket link (we have HS-123456 on file) and any additional evidence they need.

For transparency I’m including the attachments in this thread.

Best,
Naomi
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ledger-recon-202611.xlsx, metering-timestamp-sample.log, azure-invoice-202611.csv

From: Pieter van Dijk <pieter@cloudmarketplace.eu>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lars Nielsen <lars@acme-clouds.com>, Azure Marketplace Billing <billing@microsoft.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T16:48:00Z
Subject: Re: RE: Discrepancy on Nov invoice + VAT withholding

Naomi — thank you. We confirm we prefer marketplace reallocation first. I uploaded your CSV and our ticket (HS-123456) now references the corrected mapping. Azure billing acknowledged receipt and created ticket AZ-88521; they asked for the following extra evidence which I attached to the portal: (1) proof of ledger match (your workbook is fine), (2) legal entity tax IDs for both NL and UK entities, and (3) a short note from Redwood confirming the desired entity (please confirm NL entity: Redwood Inference B.V., VAT NL123456789).

We will monitor AZ-88521 and loop in procurement if they need a Docusign. If all goes well, credit memo should appear in the Jan payout. Will update you if Azure requests more.

Best,
Pieter
Billing ops | CloudMarket EU

Attachments in portal: redwood-ledger-recon-202611.xlsx (uploaded), AZ-88521-tracking.pdf (portal export)
